Based on my examination of the digest and email service design document and the individual design elements it defines, I can now identify all the architecture decision records it traces back through.

The design document `docs/design/service-digest-and-email.md` (DES-DIGEST-EMAIL) contains six design elements (DES-128 through DES-134), each citing which architecture decision record decided it:

- **DES-128** (buildDigest returns null for two different reasons) — **Decided in: ADR-016**
- **DES-129** (digest window bounded on both ends) — **Decided in: ADR-016**
- **DES-130** (listDigestRecipients and notification preference digestOnly are the same data viewed twice) — **Decided in: ADR-012**
- **DES-131** (renderDigest degrades gracefully with missing titles) — **Decided in: ADR-016**
- **DES-132** (sendEmail performs no network egress, only structured log write) — **Decided in: ADR-016**
- **DES-133** (renderEmail derives plain text from HTML) — **Decided in: ADR-016**
- **DES-134** (renderBody escapes every value to close XSS surface) — **Decided in: ADR-016**

The design document's own metadata also lists these ADRs in its `related` field: `related: [REQ-119, REQ-121, REQ-122, REQ-124, ADR-016, DES-121]`

ANSWER: docs/adr/ADR-012-feature-flag-strategies.md, docs/adr/ADR-016-interval-scheduler.md
